abstract: A Barnette graph is simple, cubic, $3$-connected, bipartite and planar. It has the global $H^{+-}$ property if, for every ordered pair of distinct edges $(e,f)$, some Hamilton cycle contains $e$ and avoids $f$. Barnette's conjecture has been proved (OpenAI, 2026; exposition by Z. Li, arXiv:2610.30490), and with it $P_2$-, $P_4$-Hamiltonicity, $H^-$ and the $H^{+-}$ condition for edge pairs at distance at most $1$ hold for every Barnette graph; global $H^{+-}$ for all Barnette graphs remains open. All Barnette graphs on at most $66$ vertices are known computationally to have it, and infinite families follow from tight-cut composition. We give a controlled expansion mechanism with an explicit growth rate. Starting from the cube, we iterate legal $C_4$-expansions at two recurrent sites. An exact six-traversal criterion describes the Hamilton cycles of one expansion in terms of parent structures. A finite signed-support invariant (22 states, or 40 when reflected orientations are allowed), initialised by explicit cube witnesses, then shows that every construction word yields a Barnette graph with global $H^{+-}$. A rooted grammar argument shows that depth $k$ produces exactly $2^{\max(k-2,0)}$ boundary-pointwise isomorphism types. A cubic embedding bound turns this into $B_{H^{+-}}(8+4k)\ge\lceil 2^{\max(k-2,0)}/((8+4k)3^{7})\rceil$, so $B_{H^{+-}}(n)\ge 2^{n/4-O(\log n)}$ along $n\equiv 0 \pmod 4$. Exhaustive computer checks agree with these statements for all standard words with $n\le 32$ and all reflected words with $n\le 28$. Limitations: the result concerns two specific expansion sites, not arbitrary $C_4$-expansions. The explicit bound first exceeds $1$ at $n=88$. A 2005 edge-replacement scheme of Kao and Chen could not be consulted in full, so we make no absolute priority claim.
author: lihongmin
change_summary:
- Section 1 and 'Related work and distinction' (v5 review): replaced 'nor does an arbitrary legal expansion preserve global H^{+-}' and 'global H^{+-} need not be preserved' by the formulation already used in 'Not claimed' (preservation of global H^{+-} under arbitrary legal C_4-expansions is not established), and described the passage before Theorem 5.7 of [2] as a limitation of the generation-based verification argument: it confirms Hamiltonicity of larger graphs from H^{+-} on smaller ones without propagating H^{+-} itself.
- Citation precision (each location checked against the cited text): [2] Theorems 1.7(iv), 5.1 and 5.7(iii) and Lemma 4.5(iv); [5] Theorem 4.1; [7] Theorems 3.6 and 3.12; [8] Theorem 8; [10] Corollary 1.13; [12] Theorem 1.7 (dual form); [4], Section 1, for Kelmans' equivalence and for the facial H^{+-} checks of [6].
- Descriptions of cited work made exact: [3] is a digested exposition of the proof in [1]; the finite verification of [5] also covers P_2-Hamiltonicity up to 78 and Hamiltonicity up to 90 vertices; [6] generates all Barnette graphs from the cube and checked facial H^{+-}-type properties for small graphs; the hypothesis of [4] is that B_1 cup B_2 and B_1 cup B_3 induce forests; [11] concerns 3-connected planar cubic graphs; [12] concerns faces with at most four neighbouring faces of size at least 6; the spider-web networks of [13], [14] form the two-parameter family SW(m,n) on mn vertices, so an order is attained by at most divisor-many members (replacing 'one graph per order').
- References: [7] corrected to Journal of Discrete Mathematical Sciences and Cryptography 26(4) (2023) 951-965 (previously the online-first pagination 1-15); issue numbers added to [2], [4], [5], [6], [9], [11], [12], [13]; arXiv identifiers added to [5] and [12]; the access note removed from entry [15] (the access limitation is still stated in the text).
- Supplement: scripts and outputs unchanged; the supplement README now notes that the JSON results file also records the base case k = 0, and a new checksum file CONTENTS.sha256 lists the SHA-256 checksums of the other eight files.
title: Exponentially Many Barnette Graphs with the Global $H^{+-}$ Property
